title: PIC Z(7)9 vs PIC 9(8) — leading-zero suppression on edit pictures only on the output side
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. EDIT-OUTPUT.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
      *> WS-AMT is a numeric field (PIC 9(8)) -- 12345 stored as
      *>   '00012345'. WS-AMT-EDIT is an edit picture; MOVE into it
      *>   produces '   12345' (5 leading spaces, last digit forced).
      *>   The DISPLAY then renders with the spaces, NOT zeros.
       01  WS-AMT          PIC 9(8).
       01  WS-AMT-EDIT     PIC Z(7)9.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           MOVE 12345 TO WS-AMT-EDIT.
           DISPLAY WS-AMT-EDIT.
           STOP RUN.
notes: Edit pictures (Z, *, $, ., ,, /) are output-side only — the underlying numeric field is unchanged. A Java port that bakes the edit format into the field's storage loses the round-trip. Surface this so the rewrite separates 'storage' from 'rendering'.
